jobs: collect pictures and charts placed on a sheet
read the colour palette from a theme part
collect cell comments with their authors
list the external connections a workbook declares
read a pivot cache's source and field names
summary: Takes one node of a workbook XML part and adds what it holds to the workbook record as it is read. A picture or chart inside a fallback block is skipped, and a theme's first two colour pairs are swapped to match the order Excel indexes colours by.

jobs: collect a pivot cache field's shared values
read the rows behind a pivot cache
read table definitions and their columns
read a pivot table's layout and measure names
map pivot cache ids to their parts
read the calculation chain's cell list
note whether dates use the 1904 system
read sheet names and their order
read the workbook's defined names
summary: Takes one node of a workbook XML part and adds what it holds to the workbook record, keeping pivot cache rows as read up to a recorded cap so they can be resolved once every part is in. The 1904 date flag applies to the whole workbook when it is set.

jobs: record each relationship a package part declares
summary: Takes one node of a package part and, when it is a relationship with a target and a type, files it under the part that declares it. The relationship id is kept because sheet references resolve through it, and the type is kept only as its last segment.

jobs: read one corner of a drawing anchor
summary: Takes the name of a corner element and reads its column, row and offsets from the anchor it sits in as numbers. Returns null when the anchor has no such corner, and a missing number reads as zero.

jobs: read a theme colour entry as hex
summary: Takes one colour entry from a theme's colour scheme and returns its hex value, using the last-colour value for a system colour. Returns null for an empty entry.

jobs: keep a pivot cache cell as index or value
summary: Takes one cell of a pivot cache record: a shared-value index is kept as an index, and a literal value is read as it is. An empty cell returns null.

jobs: give a sheet part its name and order
summary: Takes one workbook sheet entry and its position, finds the part its relationship points to, and sets that part's name, id and position. When the relationship is missing it falls back to the conventional part name, and it does nothing if no part matches.

jobs: turn parsed rows into display row records
summary: Takes one parsed row and returns its height, its hidden flag and its cells with shared strings looked up. Styles, value types, formulas and shared-formula ids go in their own maps, holding only the cells that carry each one.

jobs: resolve colours in a cell format
summary: Takes one cell format definition and returns its font, fill and border with every colour resolved to hex. A format with no font keeps a null font.

jobs: attach chart or picture data to a drawing
summary: Takes one drawing anchor and returns it marked as a chart or a picture. A chart gets its part name and its data, or a placeholder noting the data could not be read, and a picture gets the name of its media part.

jobs: shape one cell comment for output
summary: Takes one cell comment and returns its cell reference, its author's name looked up by id, and its text with the author's name prefix removed.

jobs: resolve each row of a pivot cache
summary: Takes a list of pivot cache rows, each a list of cells, and resolves every cell against the shared values of its column. Returns rows of plain values.

jobs: resolve a pivot cache cell to its value
summary: Takes a cell and its column position: a null cell stays null, a literal value is returned as it is, and an index is looked up in that column's shared values. An index past the end of the list returns null.

jobs: remove an author prefix from comment text
summary: Takes comment text and its author's name and returns the text with the leading name and colon removed and the rest trimmed. With no author, or no matching prefix, it returns the trimmed text.

jobs: resolve a relative path inside a package
summary: Takes the path of a part inside a package and a target path, and returns the full path the target names. A leading slash makes the path absolute, and dot and double-dot segments are resolved.

jobs: shift a hex colour by a tint
summary: Takes a hex colour and a tint and returns the colour moved toward white for a positive tint or toward black for a negative one. A missing colour or a zero tint returns the colour unchanged.

jobs: resolve a colour from a colour spec
summary: Takes a colour specification and the theme palette, and returns a hex colour from a direct value, an indexed palette slot, or a theme slot with its tint applied. Returns null when the specification names no colour it can read.

jobs: classify a number format code by kind
summary: Takes a number format code and its built-in id and returns general, text, duration, date, time, datetime, percent, currency or number. An elapsed-time bracket marks a duration, and the letter m alone does not count as evidence of a date.

jobs: look up a cell's number format
summary: Takes a workbook and a cell's style index and returns the format's id, its code and its kind. The code comes from the file or from the built-in table, and the result is null when the style or format is missing.

jobs: convert a spreadsheet serial day to a date
summary: Takes a serial day number and the 1904 date flag and returns the date in UTC, or null when the value is not a number. Under the 1900 system a serial below sixty is moved one day later to match the calendar's historical leap day.

jobs: pick the format section for a number's sign
summary: Takes a format code and a number and returns the section that applies: the second for a negative, the third for zero when one is present, and the first otherwise. The result also says whether a minus sign must be drawn by hand.

jobs: draw a number through a format code
summary: Takes one format section and a number and returns the text a reader would see, with percent scaling, thousands separators, decimal places and trailing-comma scaling applied. Literal text in the section is kept, and a section with no digit placeholder returns only its literal text.

jobs: draw a date through a format code
summary: Takes one date format section and a date and returns the text a reader would see, filling in year, month, day, hour, minute and second, and an am or pm marker where asked. The letter m reads as minutes beside an hour or second token and as a month everywhere else.

jobs: find the nearest date token in one direction
summary: Takes a token position and a step of one or minus one, and returns the nearest date token in that direction or an empty string if there is none. It is used to tell a month letter from a minute letter.

jobs: draw one date token
summary: Takes one token of a date format with its position and appends its drawn text to the output being built. Quoted and escaped text is copied through, and month and minute tokens are chosen by the tokens beside them.

jobs: format a cell value for display
summary: Takes a raw value, its number format and the 1904 flag and returns the text a reader would see. Text and general cells show the stored value, durations show hours, minutes and seconds, and a date with no usable code falls back to an ISO date and time.

jobs: turn a sheet into display rows
summary: Takes a sheet and its workbook and returns one object per row, holding the row number and each cell under its column letter. Cells are formatted through their number format when a workbook is given, and keep the stored value otherwise.

jobs: build one display row object
summary: Takes a row with its cells and styles and returns an object holding the row number and each cell under its column letter. With a workbook each cell is formatted through its number format, and without one the stored value is kept.

jobs: profile each column of a sheet
summary: Takes a sheet, its workbook and options for the header row, the rows to scan, the number of top values to keep and the limit for a categorical column, and returns one profile per column. The header row names the columns and is left out of the counts, and a column with a heading appears even if its cells are blank.

jobs: classify a cell's value type
summary: Takes a cell's value, its stored type code and its style index and returns text, boolean, error, date or number. A cell with no type code counts as a number only when its value parses as one.

jobs: profile the values in one column
classify a column's role from its values
summary: Takes a column index and returns counts of its filled, blank and computed cells, its distinct values, its dominant value kind or mixed, its numeric range and its most common values, along with its role. The role is tested in the order empty, constant, key, measure, categorical, then plain.

jobs: describe a cell's formatting
summary: Takes a workbook and a style index and returns the cell's emphasis, font size and colour, fill, border, alignment, wrap, indent and number format. Missing parts fall back to plain defaults, and a border counts only when at least one side is drawn.

jobs: read a constant number from a formula
summary: Takes a formula's text and returns its value when the formula is a plain number, or null for a quoted string, a cell reference or a function call. A leading equals sign is ignored.

jobs: read a constant string from a formula
summary: Takes a formula's text and returns the text inside it when the formula is a plain quoted string, or null otherwise. A leading equals sign is ignored.

jobs: test whether a rule applies to a cell
summary: Takes a conditional formatting rule and a cell and returns true or false when the cell's text or value settles the rule, or null for a rule type it cannot evaluate. Numeric comparisons use the stored value where the drawn one differs from it.

jobs: describe what a conditional format paints
summary: Takes a workbook and a differential-format index and returns the emphasis, colour, fill and border that the rule paints. Returns null when the format paints nothing.

jobs: mark cells that carry hyperlinks
summary: Takes a sheet's rows and the sheet, and attaches each hyperlink to every cell inside its range. Where ranges overlap, the link declared last wins.

jobs: lay out a sheet's cells for display
summary: Takes a sheet, its workbook and limits on rows and cells, and returns its column widths and its rows of display cells, with hidden rows skipped and merged-away cells left out. Notes, links, table and pivot roles, and pictures and charts are attached along the way, a sheet that hits a limit reports where it stopped, and a sheet with no content comes back empty.

jobs: find a column's display width in pixels
summary: Takes a zero-based column index and returns its width in pixels from the sheet's setting or its default. A hidden column returns zero.

jobs: apply conditional formats to cells
report rules that could not be decided
summary: Takes a sheet's rows and the sheet, sets each cell's paint from the first matching rule that names a format in priority order, and returns how many rules could not be evaluated. A rule marked to stop after a match ends the search for that cell.

jobs: attach notes and choice lists to cells
summary: Takes a sheet's rows, the sheet and its workbook, and gives each cell that has a comment, a field instruction or a choice list a note. A choice list is resolved once per formula and shared by the cells that use it.

jobs: resolve the options of a choice list
summary: Takes a list formula and returns its options: the entries of an inline quoted list, or the non-empty values in a referenced range on this sheet or a named one. Returns null when the reference cannot be read, names a missing sheet, or holds no values.

jobs: mark table and pivot cells by their role
summary: Takes a sheet's rows, the sheet and its workbook, and tags each cell inside a table or pivot table as header, data, total, stripe, subtotal or grand total. Filter buttons and collapse toggles are flagged where the table or pivot draws them.

jobs: give a cell's formula text
summary: Takes a sheet, a row and a column and returns the formula text the cell stores. A follower of a shared formula gets its master's text tagged with the fill index, a computed cell with no stored text gets a bare equals sign, and a cell with no formula gets an empty string.

jobs: rebuild a shared formula for a cell
summary: Takes a sheet, a row and a column and returns the cell's formula, with a follower's shared master text moved by its distance from the master cell. Returns null when the master cannot be found, and an empty string when the cell has no formula.

jobs: move cell references in formula text
summary: Takes formula text and a row and column offset, and returns the text with each relative reference moved by those amounts while absolute parts stay put. A reference moved off the sheet becomes a reference error, and text inside quotes is left alone.

jobs: shift one column letter by an offset
summary: Takes an absolute marker and a column's letters and returns the column moved by the offset, or the letters unchanged when they are absolute. Returns null when the result falls off the sheet.

jobs: shift one row number by an offset
summary: Takes an absolute marker and a row number and returns the row moved by the offset, or the number unchanged when it is absolute. Returns null when the result falls off the sheet.

jobs: rewrite references outside quoted text
summary: Takes one piece of formula text split at its quoted strings and rewrites the references in the unquoted pieces, leaving quoted pieces as they are. A string literal in a formula is never changed by a move.

jobs: move one matched reference
summary: Takes one reference the pattern matched, whether a cell, a column range or a row range, and returns it moved by the offsets. If either part falls off the sheet, the whole reference becomes a reference error.

jobs: list every note in a workbook
summary: Takes a workbook and returns one row per cell comment and per field instruction or choice list, in sheet order. A rule covering a range gives one row for the whole range, addressed at its first cell, so a long form's instructions are not repeated cell by cell.

jobs: place pictures and charts on the sheet grid
summary: Takes a sheet, its workbook and its laid-out rows and columns, and returns each picture or chart as a position and size in pixels. Anchors on rows that are not drawn are skipped, an anchor inside a merged block moves to the block's top-left cell, and items with no media or no size are dropped.

jobs: mark text that spills into empty cells
summary: Takes a row's cells and the workbook, and sets how many empty neighbouring cells each piece of text can spill into, to its left or right, according to its alignment. Numbers, wrapped text and merged cells do not spill.

jobs: test whether a cell can take spilled text
summary: Takes a column position and returns true when the cell there is empty and not part of a merge, which is the only kind of cell text can spill into. A merged cell, or a column covered by one, returns false.

jobs: list XML paths with their connection state
summary: Takes the collected paths and the set of paths a connection reaches, and returns one row per path. Each row gives the file, the path, its features, its count, and whether the path is connected and by what connection type.

jobs: describe one XML path as a row
summary: Takes one collected path and its statistics and returns a display row. The row names the file and path, lists the attributes with how many distinct values each takes, notes any text, gives the count, and names the connection type when the path is connected.

jobs: build a summary table of sheets
summary: Takes a workbook and returns one row per sheet, sorted by part key, giving its name and workbook position with counts of cells, strings, styles, formulas, merges, comments, named ranges, calc chain entries, hidden rows and columns, and pivots. Named ranges and calc chain entries are matched through the sheet's workbook position.

jobs: summarise one sheet as a row
summary: Takes a sheet's part key and returns one display row with its name, workbook order, counts of its cells, string ids, styles, formulas, merges, comments, named ranges and calc chain cells, its visibility, its hidden row and column counts, and its pivot count. Named ranges and calc chain entries are matched through the sheet's workbook position.

jobs: read the rows behind a pivot cache
summary: Takes a workbook, a cache part and an optional row limit, and returns the cache's rows as objects keyed by field name, with the field names and both the row count the part holds and the count its definition declares. Returns null when the cache has no stored rows, and marks the result truncated when the limit or the part's own cap cut the rows short.

jobs: find the last used column index
summary: Takes a sheet and returns the highest zero-based column index that holds a cell, or -1 when none does.

jobs: count hidden columns up to the last used column
summary: Takes a sheet and returns how many of its columns up to the last used one are hidden. Column ranges are read as one-based and inclusive, and a sheet with no cells returns zero.

jobs: build a table of external connections
summary: Takes a workbook and returns one row per external connection, with its id, name, kind, type code, a Power Query flag, detail and description.

jobs: describe one connection as a row
summary: Takes one connection and returns a display row with its id, name, kind, type code, a Power Query flag, detail and description. The flag is blank for any connection that is not a Power Query.

jobs: build a table of pivot tables
summary: Takes a workbook and returns one row per pivot table, in part-key order. Each row gives the table's sheet and range, its field and measure counts, and what it reads from its cache.

jobs: describe one pivot table as a row
summary: Takes a pivot table and its part name and returns a display row with its name, sheet, range, row, column and filter field counts, measure names, the source range, record count and field count of its cache, and its part name. The cache figures are blank when the cache cannot be found.

jobs: list XML paths no connection reaches
summary: Takes the collected paths and the set of connected paths, and returns a row for each path no connection reaches. Rows are sorted by category and then by occurrence count from highest to lowest, and a path's category is the extension block it sits in or else the folder of its file.

jobs: describe one unconnected path as a row
summary: Takes one unconnected path and its statistics and returns a display row with its category, file, path, occurrence count, number of attributes and whether it holds text.

jobs: build a table of workbook parts
summary: Takes the collected paths, the connected set and the sheet-connection map, and returns one row per XML part, sorted by category and then file name. Each part's row rolls up its paths, its connected paths, the sheets it touches, the connection types and its attributes.

jobs: describe one workbook part as a row
name the category of a workbook part
summary: Takes one part and its roll-up and returns a display row with its file, category, path and connected counts, sheets touched, connection types, and attributes without namespace declarations. The category is read from the file name, and an unmatched file is Relationships when it is a rels part and Other otherwise.

jobs: unpack the package inside a query blob
summary: Takes the text of an XML part and returns the format version and inner package bytes from its base64 blob, cut to the declared length when that fits the blob. Returns null when the part holds no blob, the blob cannot be decoded, or it is too short to hold its header.

jobs: read the scripts of a query blob
summary: Takes the text of an XML part holding a query blob and returns its format version and the script files inside it, each with its path and text, sorted by path. Returns null when there is no readable blob or the inner package cannot be opened.

jobs: parse a workbook package from a zip file
attach pictures and query scripts to the result
summary: Takes a zip file's contents and returns the parsed workbook from its XML and relationship parts, with each picture attached as a data URI. The query scripts are attached afterwards, from the first custom XML part that holds one, because reading them is asynchronous while the parse is not.

jobs: attach one picture as a data URI
summary: Takes one package entry and, when its file extension is a picture format a page can draw, stores it under its path as a base64 data URI. Other formats, such as EMF or WMF logos, are skipped.

jobs: define the list of extract kinds
give a cell address from its position
order a workbook's sheets by position
summary: Sets up helpers that reach the shared spreadsheet kit only when called and fail with a message naming any missing load, then lists the extract kinds, each with a label, scope, view, cheap count and rows builder. Each kind's rows builder is either written inline or cut out as its own unit.
